summary.headline: Stanley Lifestyles Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR 9,935 lakhs (from 10,861 lakhs) and PAT was just INR 65 lakhs, on delayed handovers and B2B shipment disruption.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations declined about 8.5% YoY to INR 9,935 lakhs in Q1 FY27, driven by slower retail conversions as residential handovers slipped 12 to 18 months and by B2B billing that stalled due to West Asia freight disruption. Management said gross margin was maintained and EBITDA was INR 1,722 lakhs (17.3% margin), with PAT of INR 65 lakhs. The company opened 3 Bangalore stores and closed 4 (3 Bangalore, 1 Mumbai), entered Sri Lanka via a JV, opened a Jaipur store, and announced a store-format overhaul (Stanley Superlative Living) plus a proposed amalgamation of subsidiaries. An internal audit flagged a fraud by the company secretary, under investigation.

segments.name: Retail (COCO and franchise)
segments.commentary: Customer inquiries and footfall are encouraging but conversions are slower as buyers (80-85% new premium/luxury home buyers) await possession. Network: 47 COCO stores, of which 35 are store-level EBITDA positive per management. FOFO franchisees are on a cash-and-carry model with no credit given.

segments.name: B2B / export
segments.commentary: Products are produced and held, but invoicing did not happen in Q1 due to freight and logistics disruption from the Middle East conflict; management called the B2B visibility the highest ever. US tariffs have stalled export talks, and the company is pinning hopes on BIS certification enforcement for imports from 14 August 2026.

segments.name: Sofas & More / Stanley Boutique / Stanley Level Next
segments.commentary: Average annual revenue per store: Sofas & More INR 4.5 to 6 crores; Stanley Boutique INR 4 to 6 crores; Stanley Level Next INR 10 to 14 crores (some stores up to INR 20 crores). Boutiques to be converted into Sofas & More over 2 to 3 years in the six metros.

guidance_outlook: Brand architecture change (3 brands into one Stanley and one Sofas & More) expected to complete in about 3 to 4 quarters; conversion of Boutiques to Sofas & More is gradual, taking 2 to 3 years.
Target of 15% to 20% YoY same-store growth for mature stores; Q1 SSSG was slightly negative due to format changes.
Store-level EBITDA break-even expected 6 to 12 months after opening; ROI (capital with interest) expected in 24 to 36 months.
Management says manufacturing can scale to about 2x current revenue by recalibrating the factory with a few added machines.
No explicit margin guidance given; corporate costs expected to stay roughly flat as the company adds people for the new formats.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity utilisation about 68% to 70%; over 1,000 skilled artisans said to be fully utilised.
Sofas & More capex about INR 2 crores per store (5,000 to 6,000 sq ft). Large single-city flagship stores (Stanley Superlative Living) capex up to INR 20 crores.
Hyderabad Jubilee Hills (Road No. 45) Superlative store said to be 2 to 3 weeks from opening; large-format plans for Mumbai, Bangalore and Delhi, with one city one mega store in four cities.
Q1 openings: 3 Bangalore stores (2 Varthur, 1 Mysore Road). Closures: 4 (3 Bangalore, 1 Mumbai); management said 2 of the Bangalore closures had already been relocated.
New stores: Stanley Boutique Colombo, Sri Lanka (July 2026, JV with Singer Sri Lanka PLC) and Sofas & More Jaipur (first Rajasthan store).
demand_pricing: Demand demand: customer inquiries and footfall encouraging, but conversions slowed as residential handovers were delayed 12 to 18 months in several projects; West Asia supply chain issues constrained construction material availability.
Stanley Superlative Living targets buyers with budgets of INR 3 to 5 crores and above, aiming for average ticket size up to about 10x current levels with full home design, build and install.
Management said 6 COCO cities (Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Delhi, Chennai and one other) account for about 80% of India's luxury housing, per company claim.
Sofas & More: about 95% of customers are direct buyers without designers or specifiers; Stanley relies more on specifiers and design-led purchases.
Export exposure is small; management said the business is mainly domestic and US tariffs have stalled talks with large US buyers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is depreciation about INR 15 crores per quarter (above INR 50 crores a year)?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Sudhir Iyer attributed it to Ind AS accounting; IGAAP depreciation would be lower, and the charge is front-loaded in the earlier years of asset lives. He did not give asset-class detail.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company report pre-Ind AS margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said only Ind AS numbers will be published, but pre-Ind AS figures are available offline. Management then gave pre-Ind AS averages: gross margin 56% to 60%, EBITDA margin 11% to 13%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the order book and B2B billing?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book stood at INR 68 crores on 30 June 2026, up from INR 62 crores at March 2026. Products are produced but cannot be invoiced until logistics clear.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Stanley Superlative Living format?
qa_highlights.answer: A large-format store in mature markets, replacing smaller Stanley stores. Management said Hyderabad is the proof of concept; the format consolidates Boutique and Level Next. Sofas & More becomes the value-premium brand.

qa_highlights.question: How many COCO stores are store-level EBITDA positive?
qa_highlights.answer: 35 of 42 mature COCO stores are EBITDA positive, after cash rent (the answer refers to 42 stores out of 47 total). Break-even takes 6 to 12 months and ROI 24 to 36 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are same-store sales growth and mature store revenues?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 mature-store SSSG was slightly negative due to format changes; target is 15% to 20% YoY. Average annual revenue: Sofas & More about INR 5 crores, Boutique INR 4 to 5 crores, Level Next about INR 10 crores plus.

risks_watch: Conversion recovery depends on residential handovers, which management says slipped 12 to 18 months in several projects; West Asia supply chain is constraining construction materials.
B2B billing stalled despite a record order book (INR 68 crores at 30 June 2026); watch whether logistics clear and invoicing resumes after BIS enforcement from 14 August 2026.
Internal audit found fraudulent activity by the company secretary, with misappropriation of funds acknowledged on the call; investigation outcome and disclosure pending.

Brand architecture change (Stanley Superlative Living, Boutique conversion to Sofas & More over 2 to 3 years) and store relocations/closures; execution and same-store sales recovery (Q1 mature-store SSSG slightly negative) to monitor.
Depreciation of about INR 15 crores per quarter under Ind AS, with the company declining to publish pre-Ind AS figures routinely; management did not give asset-class detail.
key_quotes: Residential project handovers have been delayed by 12 to 18 months in several cases.
As a result, while customer inquiries and store footfall remains encouraging, conversions are slower as customers await possession of their homes.

So we found that in the Q1 audit on the internal controls, so we found some fraudulent activity has been done by the company secretary, and the investigation is going on, and we will let you know to the public in short while once we complete the investigations.
We should report Ind AS numbers only. But as a CFO, I can carry to you what the IGAAP looks like offline.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on long-term demand and brand strategy but cautious on near-term trading, attributing the revenue decline to handover delays and West Asia logistics rather than demand. It was evasive on the depreciation breakdown, on export revenue figures, and on the nature of the fraud, giving only brief answers.

growth.why: Revenue fell about 8.5% YoY to INR 9,935 lakhs and net store count shrank (3 opened, 4 closed), with Q1 same-store sales slightly negative and handovers delayed 12-18 months, while B2B invoicing stalled; the company has new stores and a 15-20% same-store growth target for mature stores, but no explicit revenue growth guidance, so the outlook nets to flat.
